{{Quote|A civil war killed most of Satine's people, hence her aversion to violence. When she returned, she took on the difficult task of rebuilding her world alone.|Obi-Wan Kenobi|<ref name="Voyage of Temptation" />}}
The '''Great Clan Wars''' were a series of [[Mandalorian/Legends|Mandalorian]] inter-clan [[Ground warfare/Legends|conflicts]] that engulfed the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Mandalore/Legends|Mandalore]] over a [[Standard decade/Legends|decade]] prior to the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]]. The civil war arose from clan disputes that escalated into full-scale hostilities in the wake of the [[Mandalorian Civil War (True Mandalorians)|Mandalorian Civil War]]. Clans and even families found themselves at odds, sparking a number of battles that devastated the Mandalorian [[Homeworld/Legends|homeworld]]. The [[Death Watch/Legends|Death Watch]] splinter group soon entered the war, intending to topple the dominant [[New Mandalorians/Legends|New Mandalorian]] regime, but was unable to do so.

As the civil war ravaged Mandalore and its clans, the New Mandalorians gained a new leader: [[Duchess/Legends|Duchess]] [[Satine Kryze/Legends|Satine Kryze]], whose [[Satine Kryze's father/Legends|father]], the Duke of [[Clan Kryze/Legends|Clan Kryze]], was among the conflict's [[Death/Legends|casualties]]. The charismatic Kryze convinced most of the quarreling clan leaders and warriors to embrace pacifism, effectively ending the war. While Kryze ushered in a new age of peace and prosperity to Mandalore, the Death Watch survived into the [[Time/Legends|time]] of the Clone Wars, never relenting in its campaign to oust Kryze and [[Gender/Legends|her]] regime.

==Prelude==
For the [[Mandalorian/Legends|Mandalorian]] warrior clans, the repercussions of the [[Mandalorian Excision]] of [[738 BBY]]&mdash;in which the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] and [[Jedi Order/Legends|Jedi Order]] invaded and devastated [[Mandalore sector/Legends|Mandalorian Space]]<ref name="Warfare">''[[The Essential Guide to Warfare]]''</ref>&mdash;surpassed even the effects of the Republic's onslaught on their [[Planet/Legends|worlds]]. The pacifistic regime of the [[New Mandalorians/Legends|New Mandalorians]] ascended to power, forcing the Mandalorians' ancient [[Resol'nare|warrior traditions]] under the thumb of peace. Yet, there were some by the name of the ''[[Aka'liit]]'', translated from [[Mando'a/Legends|''Mando'a'']] as the "Faithful," who refused to let the old ways atrophy. Determined to preserve their cultural heritage, the Faithful secretly continued to pass the ancient traditions from generation to generation.<ref name="The Bounty Hunter Code" />

[[File:MandaloriansOnGalidraan-JFOS3.jpg|thumb|left|280px|The Mandalorian Civil War saw the Death Watch eradicate the True Mandalorians.]]
The following [[Standard century/Legends|centuries]] tested the unity of the Faithful, with disagreements and divisions spawning conflicts like a [[Mandalorian–Ithullan war|crusade]] against the [[Ithullan]] [[Species/Legends|species]]. The breaking point came<ref name="The Bounty Hunter Code" /> in the [[Standard year/Legends|year]] [[60 BBY/Legends|60 BBY]],<ref name="NEC" /> when two opposing factions attained prominence: the [[Supercommando Codex|reformist]] [[True Mandalorians]] and the violent and reactionary [[Death Watch/Legends|Death Watch]].<ref name="History of the Mandalorians">{{InsiderCite|80|The History of the Mandalorians: Exploring the Evolution of a Mighty Race of Warriors}}</ref> The ensuing [[Mandalorian Civil War (True Mandalorians)|Mandalorian Civil War]] [[Death/Legends|claimed many lives]], culminating with the massacre of the True Mandalorians at the [[Battle of Galidraan]]<ref name="Open Seasons 3">[[Jango Fett: Open Seasons 3|''Jango Fett: Open Seasons'' 3]]</ref> in [[44 BBY/Legends|44 BBY]].<ref name="Jedi vs. Sith">[[Jedi vs. Sith: The Essential Guide to the Force (real-life book)|''Jedi vs. Sith: The Essential Guide to the Force'']]</ref> However, the Mandalorian Civil War did little to mend some growing rifts back on [[Mandalore/Legends|Mandalore]], the heart of Mandalorian [[Realspace/Legends|Space]], where squabbles between the Mandalorian clans were rapidly escalating.<ref name="The Bounty Hunter Code" />

==The wars==
{{Quote|But even as Mereel's ideas died on Galidraan, Mandalore was in flames. The Great Clan Wars had begun. We declared ourselves and sought to rally our kinsmen to our standard, but we were too few, weakened by petty clan disputes that had flared into conflagrations while the fight with the True Mandalorians distracted us.|Tor Vizsla|<ref name="The Bounty Hunter Code" />}}
Around 44 [[Galactic Standard Calendar|BBY]],<ref name="Start Date" /> the inter-clan dissension on Mandalore reached a boiling point, erupting into all-out civil war.<ref name="The Bounty Hunter Code" /> Multiple [[Warlord/Legends|warlords]] turned on each other, with their clans and even families caught in the middle of the [[Ground warfare/Legends|crossfire]].<ref name="Shadow Conspiracy" /> Although the Death Watch, under the [[Secret Mandalore|command]] of the warrior [[Tor Vizsla]], entered the conflict in an attempt to garner public support and gain momentum for its cause, it too had suffered from the clan disputes.<ref name="The Bounty Hunter Code" /> The battles that followed resulted in many deaths and further devastation to the Mandalorian [[Homeworld/Legends|homeworld]].<ref name="Shadow Conspiracy" />

[[File:Obi-Wan_Sateen.jpg|thumb|right|280px|Satine Kryze, protected by then&ndash;Padawan Obi-Wan Kenobi, ended the Great Clan Wars.]]
Amidst the fighting, the [[Satine Kryze's father/Legends|warlord]] of [[Clan Kryze/Legends|Clan Kryze]] sent [[Gender/Legends|his]] daughter, [[Satine Kryze/Legends|Satine Kryze]], to the Republic [[Capital/Legends|capital]] of [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]] for [[Diplomat/Legends|diplomatic]] training. After her [[Parent/Legends|father]] perished in the conflict, Kryze gained [[Anti-Mandalore|leadership]] over the New Mandalorians<ref name="Shadow Conspiracy" /> and was elected as the duchess of Mandalore,<ref name="FF-2014 17: Kryze">{{FactFile2014|17|KRY 1-6|Duchess Satine Kryze}}</ref> becoming the best hope to save her clan.<ref name="Shadow Conspiracy" /> Due to her target status, the [[Jedi High Council/Legends|Jedi High Council]] assigned her two [[Bodyguard/Legends|bodyguards]] for her return to the embattled Mandalore: [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Master]] [[Qui-Gon Jinn/Legends|Qui-Gon Jinn]] and his [[Padawan/Legends|Padawan]], [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]]. Jinn and Kenobi's mission to protect Kryze lasted a full year, as the insurgents opposed to her rule sent [[Bounty hunter/Legends|bounty hunters]] after the young duchess.<ref name="Voyage of Temptation" />

Kryze and her [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] allies were forced off-world at [[Time/Legends|times]], taking refuge on nearby planets such as [[Draboon/Legends|Draboon]], another world in Mandalorian Space.<ref name="Voyage of Temptation" /><ref name="TEAOC">{{SW|url=news/star-wars-the-essential-atlas-online-companion|text=''Star Wars: The Essential Atlas'' Online Companion|int=Star Wars: The Essential Atlas Online Companion}}</ref> Kryze and Kenobi's shared time together shaped a budding romance between the two, a bond that was complicated by their greater commitments.<ref name="Voyage of Temptation" /> Ultimately, Kryze was able to convince the majority of the war-weary clan [[Chief/Legends|chieftains]] and warriors to adopt the pacifism of her regime, ending all hostilities<ref name="Shadow Conspiracy" /> prior to [[32 BBY/Legends|32 BBY]].<ref name="End Date" />

==Aftermath==
{{Quote|Satine is weak-minded, like a child, with a child's faith in goodness and rationality. She has proved all too ready to believe the exiles have given up their fight. In fact, the Death Watch is being rebuilt. As always, our trials have made us stronger.|Tor Vizsla|<ref name="The Bounty Hunter Code" />}}
[[File:PreVizslaDeathWatch-TheMandalorePlot.jpg|thumb|left|250px|Though defeated, the Death Watch kept working against the New Mandalorians.]]
The Great Clan Wars, as the event came to be known, became reputed as the deadliest conflict on Mandalore since the Mandalorian Excision of centuries prior.<ref name="Shadow Conspiracy" /> Kryze shouldered the burden of rebuilding her world alone,<ref name="Voyage of Temptation" /> as Jinn and Kenobi only briefly stayed on-world to observe the situation for the Republic<ref name="Shadow Conspiracy" /> before new orders sent them elsewhere.<ref name="Voyage of Temptation" /> Determined to never repeat the madness of the Great Clan Wars, Kryze worked with her New Mandalorian allies to ensure that Mandalore once again rejected violence as it had in the wake of the Excision, thus fostering a new age of growth and prosperity for her people.<ref name="Shadow Conspiracy" /> As part of her reforms, Kryze discouraged the traditional clan system in favor of a more democratic government.<ref name="FF-2014 17: Kryze" /> She also restructured the [[Mandalorian Guard/Legends|Mandalorian Guard]], Mandalore's primary [[Law enforcement agency/Legends|law enforcement]], because Guardsmen units had primarily become power bases for various clans.<ref name="The Bounty Hunter Code" />

The Death Watch seethed with frustration from its failure to unseat the New Mandalorians. Nevertheless, the Death Watchmen bode their time,<ref name="Shadow Conspiracy" /> their beliefs surviving in particular among the unrepentant warriors who were [[Exile (punishment)/Legends|exiled]] to Mandalore's [[Moon/Legends|moon]], [[Concordia/Legends|Concordia]].<ref name="Warfare" /><ref name="The Mandalore Plot">{{TCW|The Mandalore Plot}}</ref> Tor Vizsla recorded the Great Clan Wars in a [[Ba'jurne Kyr'tsad Mando'ad|Death Watch manifesto]] that he authored. The rise of his successor,<ref name="The Bounty Hunter Code" /> [[Pre Vizsla/Legends|Pre Vizsla]], ensured that the Death Watch continued its campaign against Kryze's New Mandalorians well into the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]] over a [[Standard decade/Legends|decade]] later.<ref name="The Mandalore Plot" />

==Behind the scenes==
The Great Clan Wars<ref name="Shadow Conspiracy" /> were created for "[[Voyage of Temptation]]," a [[2010]] episode in the [[Star Wars: The Clone Wars|''Star Wars: The Clone Wars'' television series']] [[The Clone Wars: Season Two|second season]], in which they were mentioned in passing as a "civil war" connected to Obi-Wan Kenobi's relationship with Satine Kryze.<ref name="Voyage of Temptation" /> [[:File:YoungSatine.jpg|A trading card]] from [[2011]]'s ''[[2011 Topps Star Wars Galaxy Series 6]]'', drawn by artist [[Grant Gould]], was the first source to depict the conflict, illustrating Kenobi and Qui-Gon Jinn's efforts to protect Kryze during the war.<ref name="Galaxy Series 6">{{Topps|set=2011 Topps Star Wars Galaxy Series 6|subset=Artist Sketch Cards|cardname=Grant Gould}}</ref>

In the episode, the conflict was merely identified as a "civil war,"<ref name="Voyage of Temptation" /> which left it open to interpretation as to whether it was a reference to the Mandalorian Civil War from the [[2002]] [[Star Wars comic books|comic]] [[Star Wars: Jango Fett: Open Seasons|''Jango Fett: Open Seasons'']]<ref name="Open Seasons 3" /> or an entirely new event. It was confirmed to be the latter in [[Jason Fry]]'s [[2012]] young readers' book [[The Clone Wars: Darth Maul: Shadow Conspiracy|''Darth Maul: Shadow Conspiracy'']], which named and detailed the conflict.<ref name="Shadow Conspiracy" /> Further information on the event has since been published in [[2013]]'s ''[[The Bounty Hunter Code: From the Files of Boba Fett]]''.<ref name="The Bounty Hunter Code" />

[[The Official Star Wars Fact File Part 17|''The Official Star Wars Fact File'' Part 17]], released in [[2014]], contradicted much of the information from ''The Bounty Hunter Code''. Instead of depicting Kryze's rise to power during the Great Clan Wars, ''The Official Star Wars Fact File'' placed her ascension during the twenty-six years of the preceding Mandalorian Civil War, with no direct reference to the Great Clan Wars.<ref name="FF-2014 17: Kryze" /> Due to the timeline of events established in ''The Bounty Hunter Code'', this article assumes that ''The Official Star Wars Fact File'' is in error.
